briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Flexes Despite the Tax Squeeze as National Cannabis Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis culture is still winning awards and holding demand even as the 24% wholesale tax bites, with a gubernatorial candidate now promising relief and cheap real estate opening doors for expansion. Nationally, rescheduling hit a procedural speed bump, but Wall Street uplistings, M&A, and FDA psychedelic breakthroughs keep the sector's momentum pointed up.

local.text: Hytek, Mitten Canna crowned Zalympix champions — Detroit-based Hytek's Oishii Piña took best overall live rosin while Mitten Canna Co.'s Toad Venom won best overall flower at Michigan's 2026 'Grammys of Cannabis.'
Gubernatorial candidate pledges to repeal wholesale tax — Republican John James, backed by roughly $90,000 in industry donations, has promised to cut Michigan's 24% wholesale tax if elected.
Demand holds steady despite the new 24% levy — Flower prices remain near all-time lows at Michigan dispensaries, and the feared post-tax sales collapse has not materialized two months into 2026.

Cannabis real estate now selling at fire-sale prices — At least 50 Michigan cultivation properties are listed for sale or lease, with brokers reporting deals at 20-30 cents on the dollar for operators ready to expand.

CRA hands down record $2M fines, tightens enforcement — Regulators revoked 20 grower licenses from a mid-Michigan company for shipping dirt labeled as flower, part of a tougher compliance push that rewards operators playing by the rules.

national.text: DEA rescheduling paused, but investor confidence holds firm — A judge stayed the hearing to weigh a GAO report on scheduling gaps, yet the report didn't challenge the science behind Schedule III, and surveyed investors still put 65% odds on rescheduling within six months.
Trulieve becomes first MSO to uplist to the NYSE — The cannabis giant began trading as TRLV, a move CEO Kim Rivers called a 'historic milestone' tied to the Schedule III shift.
Vireo Growth snaps up Planet 13 in all-stock deal — The acquisition adds 36 dispensaries across three states, extending one of cannabis's most aggressive consolidation sprees.
Cresco Labs lands $50M non-dilutive credit line — Needham Bank's financing gives the MSO fuel for acquisitions and positions it for a future senior-exchange uplisting.

FDA psychedelic framework pushes Compass Pathways forward — The agency's new trial-design guidance arrives as Compass's Phase 3 psilocybin program for depression posts 52-week open-label data, part of a broader federal push that could yield the first psychedelic approval within the year.
national.source: Clinical Trial Vanguard / Houston Public Media
